Unit 10 • SL

Binary Logic & Circuits

Introduction

How do binary values and logic circuits become real system decisions?

This unit links number representation, Boolean logic, and operating-system control. You will convert between number systems, describe logic-gate behavior, construct logic diagrams, and compare process scheduling strategies.

You will describe binary/decimal/hex representation, describe purpose and use of logic gates, construct logic diagrams from Boolean expressions, describe the operating system role, and compare FCFS, Round Robin, and Priority scheduling.

Data representation

Computers represent all values using binary patterns.

  • Binary: machine-level state representation.
  • Hexadecimal: compact readable form of binary.
  • Decimal: human-facing arithmetic representation.

Logic gates and diagrams

Boolean logic is implemented physically through gate circuits.

  • Core gates: AND, OR, NOT.
  • Derived gates: NAND, NOR, XOR, XNOR.
  • Construction flow: expression to diagram to verification.

Operating system role

The OS coordinates hardware resources and user/application access.

  • CPU/process management for concurrent tasks.
  • Memory and device management through controlled access.
  • File and interface services for usable systems.

Scheduling trade-offs

Scheduling determines responsiveness and fairness under load.

  • FCFS: simple queue order.
  • Round Robin: fixed time slices for fairness.
  • Priority: urgency-based service with starvation risk.

Key Terminology
TermDefinition
Binary / Decimal / HexadecimalBase-2, base-10, and base-16 number systems used for representation and conversion.
Logic gateHardware element implementing a Boolean function on binary inputs.
Boolean expressionLogical statement combining variables with operators such as AND/OR/NOT.
Truth tableTable of outputs for every possible input combination.
Logic diagramCircuit layout showing signal flow through gates.
Operating systemSystem software managing CPU, memory, peripherals, and user interaction.
SchedulingMethod used by the OS to allocate CPU time among processes.
FCFSFirst Come First Served non-preemptive scheduling policy.
Round RobinPreemptive policy rotating processes using a fixed time quantum.
Priority schedulingPolicy selecting process order by priority level.

Common Misconceptions

Hexadecimal is a different kind of data

Hex is another representation of the same binary value, not a separate data type.

XOR behaves like OR

XOR is true only when exactly one input is true.

Fastest scheduler is always best

Scheduling choice depends on fairness, responsiveness, and workload requirements.

Think Deeper

"What matters more in scheduling: fairness, speed, or predictability?" Different systems choose different priorities, so performance quality depends on context and constraints.
